title: I Tried to Prompt a 3D DEV Library Into Existence. Then I Had to Build My Own Level Editor.
why_read: A hackathon submission describing an experimental 3D spatial browser for DEV articles, more of a creative demo than a technically rigorous project.
analysis: The author describes building 'Oniria,' a 3D virtual library where DEV.to articles are represented as books on shelves that a user can walk through, built using Sanity as a backend for content and spatial memory. It grew out of an attempt to use AI to generate a 3D library tool, which failed, leading the author to build a custom level editor instead. This is an interesting creative experiment in alternative content browsing, but it reads mainly as a fun hackathon project rather than something offering broadly applicable engineering lessons. The idea of 'information as geography' is a neat concept, though the practical utility and technical depth of the writeup itself seem limited.
